findings: The planner's argument (programme/roadmap.toml, the target's evidence) checks against the definitions in Causal/Properties.lean with no gap. Take V ∈ 𝓝 p with CausallyConvexIn V ⊤, O := interior V and H := J⁺_⊤ O ∩ J⁻_⊤ O. Then p ∈ O ⊆ H by reflexivity (subset_Jplus_top_inter_Jminus_top, :115). H ⊆ V: z ∈ H gives a ≤_M z ≤_M b with a, b ∈ O ⊆ V, so z ∈ diamond ⊤ a b ⊆ V (CausallyConvexIn.Jplus_top_inter_Jminus_top_subset, :139). H is causally convex in M by transitivity, and this holds for the hull of ANY set (causallyConvexIn_Jplus_top_inter_Jminus_top, :121). H is open when J^±_⊤(O) are. The step 'z ∈ diamond ⊤ a b ⊆ V' reads CausallyConvexIn V ⊤ exactly as defined (diamond in U = ⊤ between two points of V). V itself need not be open, which is DEC-7's reading of StronglyCausal.

A cleaner characterisation, proved (causallyConvexIn_top_iff, :129): a set V is causally convex in M iff J⁺_M(V) ∩ J⁻_M(V) ⊆ V, that is, iff V is its own hull. The planner's 'V = J⁺_M(V) ∩ J⁻_M(V)' is therefore the definition, read through the hull.
questions: Does the future form causally_open_future alone suffice for strongly_causal ⇒ strongly_causal_open? This is not settled. The proof uses both halves, at U = M only. The future half alone does not make the argument's hull open: on the one-way membrane (causally open in the future, strongly causal, not causally open), take V = {−1 < u < 3, 0 < v < 4, u ≤ v}, a neighbourhood of (0,1) that is causally convex in M. The hull J⁺_M(˚V) ∩ J⁻_M(˚V) contains the membrane point (1,1) and no point (1+ε, 1) of R, so it is not open (Causal.oneWayMembrane_hull_not_isOpen, :295). The membrane is StronglyCausalOpen all the same (by balls, oneWayMembrane_stronglyCausalOpen). So this refutes the argument, not the statement. A counterexample to 'strongly_causal ∧ causally_open_future ⇒ strongly_causal_open' would itself separate the open pair strongly_causal → strongly_causal_open. The reading taken: the ladder witness takes the two-sided node, as DEC-163 asks, and its docstring says so.

findings: The planner's remark is stated with content, not as a bare contrapositive (exists_not_isOpen_hull, :212). Let C be strongly causal and not StronglyCausalOpen. Then there are a point p and a neighbourhood N ∈ 𝓝 p with three properties. (i) Some open O ∋ p has its hull J⁺_M(O) ∩ J⁻_M(O) inside N (O = the interior of a causally convex neighbourhood in N), so (ii) is not vacuous. (ii) The hull of EVERY open O ∋ p whose hull lies in N is not open. (iii) No open W ∋ p inside N contains its own hull: the planner's 'regress'. Tarentin plays no role. The ladder's form (not_causallyOpen_of_not_stronglyCausalOpen, :233): such a C is not causally open, and not even causally open at M (¬ ∀ O open, J⁺_M(O) and J⁻_M(O) open).

kb_proposals: Strong causality gives the open form under causal openness at M alone, with no tarentin: J⁺_M(O) ∩ J⁻_M(O), for O the interior of a causally convex neighbourhood, is the open convex neighbourhood. Witness StronglyCausal.stronglyCausalOpen_of_causallyOpen; weaker forms _of_isOpen_Jplus_Jminus and _of_isOpen_hull (T-abs-sc-open-without-tarentin).
A set is causally convex in M iff it contains its causal hull J⁺_M(V) ∩ J⁻_M(V) (causallyConvexIn_top_iff). The hull of any set is causally convex (causallyConvexIn_Jplus_top_inter_Jminus_top).

kb/0117 sharpened: E₀'s StronglyCausalOpen follows generically from its strong causality and E0.isOpen_Jplus / E0.isOpen_Jminus through StronglyCausal.stronglyCausalOpen_of_isOpen_Jplus_Jminus, which asks openness at U = ⊤ only.

The hull argument needs J⁻-openness. On the one-way membrane the hull of the interior of a causally convex neighbourhood is not open (oneWayMembrane_hull_not_isOpen), yet the membrane is StronglyCausalOpen: whether causally_open_future suffices for SC ⇒ SCO is open.

The isolated line (kb/0050) is strongly causal: every order-convex set of ℝ is causally convex in M (isolatedLine_causallyConvexIn_Icc). It is a cheap non-tarentin witness for theorems that take strong causality and causal openness.
